title: Florida women's swimming earns three Second-Team All-America honors at NCAA Championships
text:
Anthony Nesty, Head Coach at Florida Gators Women's Swimming & Diving | https://floridagators.com/
Anthony Nesty, Head Coach at Florida Gators Women's Swimming & Diving | https://floridagators.com/
Florida's women's swimming and diving team earned three Second-Team All-America honors on March 18 during the first day of the 2026 NCAA Division I Championships at the McAuley Aquatic Center in Atlanta, Georgia. After three events, Florida ranked 11th in the team standings with a total of 31 points.
The event structure this year featured morning preliminary times determining both individual and relay event scores, with only the top-eight swimmers, divers, and relay teams advancing to the finals session. The Gators' performance included a strong showing in both individual and relay events.
In the 1,650 freestyle, Mattes posted a time of 15:59.35—the second-fastest of the morning—and finished tenth overall to secure her second career All-America honor. Another Florida swimmer also competed in the mile event, placing twenty-second with a time of 16:14.09.
The Gators' 200 medley relay team won their heat with a time of 1:35.33 and entered finals ranked fourth but ultimately finished eleventh overall. This result placed them among the top sixteen for twelve points and earned them Second-Team All-America recognition. Their finish also marked the seventh-fastest time in University of Florida history for this event.
Florida's 800 free relay team continued to improve upon their seeding by finishing third in their morning heat with a time of 7:00.22 and moving up from fourteenth seed to eleventh place overall. This performance doubled their projected points to twelve and secured another set of Second-Team All-American honors for the squad.
Looking ahead, individual swimming and diving events will continue tomorrow with heats beginning at 10 a.m., followed by diving preliminaries at 12:15 p.m., and finals sessions scheduled for later in the evening. Fans can follow live coverage through ESPN+ or access live scoring via Meet Mobile app, Dive Meets, or through links provided on FloridaGators.com.
